feedback: The baseline (entityR2B, iteration 0, score 57.10) finished 0 of 60 trials on all three tracks. Every run ended off track after 1 to 2 line-loss events, with max_error of about 0.063 to 0.065 m against the 0.06 m limit, and progress of only 0.12 to 0.16. Steering oscillation was low (0.11 to 0.16), so the failure is a steady drift away from the line rather than jitter. The candidate responds to this with three changes: wider sensor spread (x = ±0.024 m), a larger footprint (0.016 m), and kd raised from 0.15 to 0.30. Its base_speed falls from 1.6 to 1.5. Those changes fit the evidence and the candidate is valid: the weights are antisymmetric, the sensor positions are inside the allowed range, and line_loss is last_direction. I have no measured result for it yet. The main risk is that 1.5 is the minimum speed that can still finish in 3 s, so a completion may depend on the speed/time trade-off. This is early exploration with ten iterations left, and the candidate is a clear improvement in the direction the data points, so it should race now. After the race, check first whether line_loss_events fell from 1 to 2 per run. If max_error is still above 0.06 but line losses are down, raise kp in small steps (3.0 to 3.5) before touching speed. If the run finishes but completion_time is close to 3.0 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 to 0.2. If oscillation rises after kd 0.3, go back toward kd 0.2.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are still 1 or more and max_error stays above 0.06, try kp 3.5 with kd 0.3, keeping the widened sensor spread, to cut the drift on bends.
If the run completes but completion_time is near 3.0 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 to 0.2 (1.5 to 1.7), keeping kd 0.3 so the faster robot stays damped.
If steering_oscillation rises well above the baseline 0.11 to 0.16 after kd 0.3, reduce kd to 0.2 before changing kp.
